findings.message: Appending `| tr -d ' '` makes `tr` the pipeline's exit status, so `|| echo 0` can no longer fire when `wc` fails. The fallback is dead code and a failed count comes back as an empty string instead of 0. Same at the `total=` line near 332. Capture `wc` output first and strip the padding with parameter expansion, e.g. `n=$(wc -l < f 2>/dev/null) || n=0; n=${n//[[:space:]]/}`. This only matters if the script does not use `pipefail`, which the diff does not show.
findings.scenario: `wc` fails (unreadable log) -> `local_total` is '' rather than '0'. Today `[[ '' -gt N ]]` evaluates as 0, so output looks the same, but the explicit fallback no longer works.

findings.message: The timeout/gtimeout/perl-alarm fallback is now written three times: `bounded5` in specclaw-browser-lock, `bounded10` in this test, and the existing one in specclaw-update-status, as the browser-lock comment says. The copies can disagree. For example, `timeout` exits 124 on expiry but the perl alarm path exits via SIGALRM (142), and the parser-test comment still says it detects a hang by exit 124. Put the helper in one shared sourced file and take the seconds as an argument.
findings.scenario: On macOS without gtimeout, a hung `verify collect` is killed by the perl alarm and exits 142. Any check for 124 would miss it, while the same hang on Linux reports 124.
